item.title: On the Moduli Difference of Initial Logarithmic and Inverse Logarithmic Coefficients of Ma-Minda Convex Functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.20645v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}(\Phi)$ denote a subclass of class $ \mathcal{C}$ of convex functions in the unit disc $\mathbb{D}=\{z:|z|<1, z\in \mathbb{C}\}$ defined by \begin{equation*} {Re}\left \{1+ \frac{ zf^{\prime \prime}(z)}{f^{\prime}(z)}\right \} \prec \Phi(z), \end{equation*} where $\Phi$ represents the Ma--Minda function in $\mathbb{D}$. For $f\in\mathcal{C}(\Phi)$, we find the sharp estimates of $||\gamma_{2}|-|\gamma_{1}||$, where $\gamma_{1}$ and $\gamma_{2}$ are the first two logarithmic coefficients of $f$. The bound is also obtained for the inverse logarithmic coefficients $\Gamma_{1}$ and $\Gamma_{2}$. We then show that, under suitable conditions, the bounds for $||\gamma_{2}|-|\gamma_{1}||$ and $||\Gamma_{2}|-|\Gamma_{1}||$ are identical, which gives the invariance result between these functionals. We also present bounds for the differences for various classes of univalent functions by choosing particular function $\Phi$. Thus our results unify several results studied in the literature.
item.dc:creator: Rashid Ali, Mohsan Raza, Umar Raza

item.title: Directional Coefficient Inequalities for Strongly Starlike Mappings in Complex Banach Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.20849v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a class of strongly starlike mappings of order $\alpha$ on the open unit ball of a complex Banach space under a scalar-profile condition. Using a slice reduction along one-dimensional complex subspaces, we prove a coefficient correspondence theorem identifying the directional coefficients with the Taylor coefficients of an associated one-variable strongly starlike function. We further prove a lifting theorem showing that every one-variable strongly starlike function can be realized by a scalar-profile Banach-space mapping. Consequently, the extremal problems for polynomial directional coefficient functionals coincide exactly with their one-variable counterparts. We apply this correspondence to obtain bounds for $|A_2A_3 - A_4|$, $|A_2A_4 - A_3^2|$, and $|A_3 - A_2^2|$, together with the corresponding estimates for $|A_4|$ and $|A_5|$. We also establish a parameterized Fekete--Szeg\H{o} estimate and a sharp bound for the second Hankel determinant of directional logarithmic coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Pradip Das, Nabadwip Sarkar

item.title: Length control for foliations by Jordan curves via smooth quasiconformal maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.21009v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\Omega\subsetneq\mathbb C$ be a non-empty simply connected domain and $0<p<2$. Bouchala and Koskela [Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (2024)] proved that there exists a quasiconformal map $f:\mathbb D\to\Omega$ such that $\int_0^1\ell(f(r S^1))^p\,dr<\infty$, and asked whether this conclusion holds at $p=2$, or even for every $0<p<2+\varepsilon$ with some $\varepsilon>0$. We answer this question affirmatively with $\varepsilon=2/157$ by constructing a single smooth $5$-quasiconformal map $f:\mathbb D\to\Omega$ satisfying this integrability condition simultaneously for every $0<p<2+2/157$.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Pandey

item.title: Oka-Weil approximation theorem for polynomials with exponents in compact convex sets in $\mathbb R^n$
item.description: arXiv:2610.21181v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $S\subset\R^n_+$ be a compact convex set with $0\in S$, and let $\cP^S$ be the ring of polynomials whose exponents of the $m$-th degree lie in the dilates $mS$. Sigur{\dh}ard\'ottir proved an Oka--Weil theorem for compact $\cP^S$-convex subsets of $(\C^*)^n$ and asked whether it holds for all compact $\cP^S$-convex subsets of $\C^n$. We answer this question affirmatively when the cone $\R_+S$ is rational polyhedral, for every $S$ when $n=2$, and for several classes of nonpolyhedral cones in all dimensions; in all these cases the compact sets may meet the coordinate hyperplanes. For arbitrary $S$ we prove that the Oka--Weil property of a compact $\cP^S$-convex set is equivalent to the compactness of its hull with respect to a finitely generated monomial subring of $\cP^S$, to a corona-type certificate, and to the existence of a bounded neighbourhood defined by finitely many inequalities $|p_j|<c_j$ with $p_j\in\cP^S$. The proofs use monomial charts, the classical Oka--Weil theorem in an auxiliary affine space, and elementary Gelfand theory. As applications we obtain an Oka--Stolzenberg criterion for $\cP^S$-hulls and the corresponding rational approximation theorem.
item.dc:creator: Duong Thi Thuy Van, Kieu Phuong Chi

item.title: On coefficient theorems for starlike and quasi-convex of type B mappings in complex Banach spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.21255v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study biholomorphic mappings $F: \mathbb{B} \to X$ of the form $F(z) = f(z)z$ for $z \in \mathbb{B}$, where $f: \mathbb{B} \to \mathbb{C}$ is a holomorphic function satisfying $f(0) = 1$ and $X$ is a complex Banach space with the unit ball $\mathbb{B}$. The main contributions of this paper are threefold. First, we establish a sufficient coefficient condition for a function $F(z)=zf(z)$ to be starlike and quasi-convex of type $B$ in a complex Banach space. Second, we prove that the Bieberbach conjecture holds for these classes of functions. Finally, we analyze the difference of coefficients for such functions in this setting. The results established here directly extend the previous results to the broader setting of complex Banach spaces.
item.dc:creator: Janusz Sokol, Sujoy Majumder, Goutam Haldar

item.title: Alpha-convex functions in complex Banach spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.21260v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathbb{B}$ be the unit ball in a complex Banach space ${\mathbb X}$. We study biholomorphic mappings $F: \mathbb{B} \to {\mathbb X}$ of the form $F(z) = f(z)z$ for $z \in \mathbb{B}$, where $f: \mathbb{B} \to \mathbb{C}$ is a holomorphic function satisfying $f(0) = 1$. Our main contributions are as follows: Inclusion Results: We establish inclusion conditions for $\mathcal{M}_{\alpha}(\mathbb{B})$, class of $\alpha$-convex functions in $\mathbb{B}$ to belong to the classes of starlike mappings or quasi-convex mappings of type $B$ on $\mathbb{B}$ for specified ranges of $\alpha$. Characterization: We prove that $F(z) = \frac{f(l_{u}(z))}{l_{u}(z)}z \in \mathcal{M}_{\alpha}(\mathbb{B})$ if and only if $f \in \mathcal{M}_{\alpha}(\mathbb{U})$, where $f \in \mathcal{S}(\mathbb{U})$, $u \in {\mathbb X}$ with $\|u\| = 1$, and $l_{u} \in T(u)$. Duality: We present a duality relationship between the classes $\mathcal{S}^*(\mathbb{U})$ and $\mathcal{M}_{\alpha}(\mathbb{B})$ for $\alpha \ge 0$. Hankel Determinant Bounds: We determine sharp upper bounds for the second Hankel determinant of mappings in $\mathcal{M}_\alpha(\mathbb{B})$ when $\alpha \ge 0$. The results established here directly extend the previous results to the broader setting of complex Banach spaces.
item.dc:creator: Janusz Sokol, Sujoy Majumder, Goutam Halder

item.title: Smale's mean value constant and admissible univalent Blaschke pairs
item.description: arXiv:2610.21472v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be the class of polynomials $P$ of degree at least $2$ with $P(0)=0$, $P'(0)=1$, let $S(P)=\min_{P'(c)=0}|P(c)/c|$ and let $\mathcal{M}=\sup_{P\in\mathcal{P}}S(P)$ be Smale's mean value constant. Smale proved that $\mathcal{M}\le4$, observed that $\mathcal{M}\ge 1$, and asked whether $\mathcal{M}=1$. We show that $\mathcal{M}$ coincides with $$ \mathcal{B}=\sup\frac1{B(0)}, $$ the supremum running over pairs $(W,B)$ in which $W$ is a normalised univalent map of the standard unit disk $\mathbb{D}$ and $B$ is a finite Blaschke product with $B(0)>0$ such that $WB$ is locally univalent in $\mathbb{D}$. Smale's question is therefore a problem in univalent function theory. We also introduce the degree-restricted constants $\mathcal{B}_d$ for $B$ with $\mathrm{deg} B \le d$ and show that $$1.1018586788\ldots=\sqrt{\frac{8081}{6656}} \le \mathcal{B}_1 < \sqrt{\frac{7}{5}}=1.1832159566\ldots$$ This implies that $\mathcal{M}>1.1018$ and we also show that there are polynomials of arbitrarily large degree with $S(P)>1.1018$.
item.dc:creator: Aneesh Jatar, Tuen Wai Ng

item.title: Resolutions of compact balanced spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.21728v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X$ be a compact reduced balanced complex space of pure dimension $n\geq2$. We prove that every resolution of singularities of $X$ is a balanced manifold; in particular, $X$ belongs to the class $\mathscr{B}$. This removes the additional cohomological assumptions appearing in earlier results of Fu-Meng-Xia. The main new ingredient is the linear independence of the Aeppli classes of the exceptional prime divisors of a projective bimeromorphic morphism onto a normal complex space. This follows from the vanishing of curve degrees for Aeppli-trivial divisors and the relative negativity lemma. For non-normal spaces, strict positivity is used to eliminate divisors mapping onto codimension-one subsets before passing to the normalization. We also recall a classical surface example of Grauert showing that the inclusion of compact balanced spaces in $\mathscr{B}$ is strict.
item.dc:creator: Jixiang Fu, Wei Xia

item.title: Pseudoconvex domains in complex Euclidean space with one-dimensional Bergman spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.21749v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For any $n \geq 2$, we construct a pseudoconvex domain in $\C^n$ such that the Bergman space is one-dimensional. This disproves Wiegerinck conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Yuan

item.title: Unimodular Zeros of Selmer's Harmonic Trinomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.22132v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $n>k$ be positive integers and let $\varepsilon,\delta\in\{-1,1\}$. In this note, we classify the unimodular zeros of the harmonic trinomial $H_{\varepsilon,\delta}:\mathbb{C}\to \mathbb{C}$ given by \[ H_{\varepsilon,\delta}(z)=z^n+\varepsilon\overline z^{\,k}+\delta, \] where $\overline{z}$ is the complex conjugate of $z\in \mathbb{C}$. Let $g:=\gcd(n,k)$ be the greatest common divisor of $n$ and $k$, and set $n_0:=n/g$ and $k_0:=k/g$. For each choice of $\varepsilon,\delta\in \{-1,1\}$, we give a necessary and sufficient congruence involving $n_0$ and $k_0$ to guarantee that $H_{\varepsilon,\delta}$ has unimodular zeros. More precisely, if the corresponding congruence holds, then $H_{\varepsilon,\delta}$ has exactly $2g$ unimodular zeros, which are given explicitly; otherwise, it has no unimodular zeros. The proof uses a reduction to a trinomial equation and elementary divisibility arguments.
item.dc:creator: Gerardo Barrera, Waldemar Barrera, Juan Pablo Navarrete

item.title: Understanding entropy using Aubin--Yau deformations
item.description: arXiv:2610.21198v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper we investigate three types of entropy that frequently appear in the research of K\"ahler geometry: the classical K\"ahler entropy, the radial entropy and the non-Archimedean entropy. We give a unifying interpretation for these entropies by showing that they can all be expressed as the derivative of the Monge--Amp\`ere energy along certain Aubin--Yau type deformations. Such considerations also lead to a novel algebraic criterion for the existence of constant scalar curvature K\"ahler metrics.
item.dc:creator: Tam\'as Darvas, Kewei Zhang

item.title: The space of polarized compactifications of an affine variety
item.description: arXiv:2610.21838v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $X$ be a normal affine variety over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Through the lens of non-Archimedean geometry, we study the space of polarized compactifications of $X$, consisting of pairs $(\bar X, D)$ where $\bar X$ is a normal projective variety containing $X$ as a dense open subset, and $D$ is an effective ample $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor with support equal to the complement of $X$ in $\bar X$. We identify this space with a natural class of functions--the Fubini--Study functions--on the Berkovich analytification of $X$. Through a Rees correspondence, we also give a bijection with the space of homogeneous $\mathbb{Q}$-valued, finitely generated negative non-Archimedean norms (or filtrations) on the coordinate ring of $X$. Using the above identifications, we equip the space of polarized compactifications, and numerical classes thereof, with natural metrics and identify the metric completions. The latter include a space of continuous plurisubharmonic functions in the sense of Chambert-Loir and Ducros, and a space of birational curve classes as studied by Dang and Favre.
item.dc:creator: Mattias Jonsson, Yueqiao Wu

item.title: Volterra operators on the BMOA space of Dirichlet series
item.description: arXiv:2610.21873v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we completely characterize the boundedness and compactness of Volterra operators on \(BMOA_{\mathcal D}\), the BMOA space of Dirichlet series, and estimate their essential and weak essential norms. We further prove that compactness, weak compactness, and complete continuity are equivalent for these operators. In particular, every Dirichlet polynomial symbol induces a compact Volterra operator on \(BMOA_{\mathcal D}\). We also prove that every such symbol induces a compact Volterra operator on the Bergman space of Dirichlet series \(\mathcal A_\mu^1\) for every admissible measure \(\mu\), extending the corresponding compactness theorem, previously established for \(1<p<\infty\), to the endpoint \(p=1\).
item.dc:creator: Cezhong Tong, Maofa Wang, Zixing Yuan

item.title: Uniformization of Julia sets of geometrically finite rational maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.21945v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A Schottky set is the complement of a collection of disjoint open disks in the Riemann sphere. We completely characterize geometrically finite rational maps whose Julia sets are quasiconformally equivalent to Schottky sets. We also prove that the closure of the basin of infinity of a geometrically finite unicritical polynomial is quasiconformally equivalent to a Schottky set if and only if either there exists an attracting cycle and all bounded Fatou components have disjoint closures or there exists a parabolic cycle of multiplicity three. An ingredient of the proof is a new dynamical characterization of pairs of arbitrary quasicircles that are quasiconformally equivalent to pairs of tangent circles.
item.dc:creator: Yusheng Luo, Dimitrios Ntalampekos

item.title: Extending Donaldson's HyperK\"ahler Structure via Minimal Surfaces into $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{C})$
item.description: arXiv:2610.22288v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a deformation space for minimal immersions into $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{C})$ with its holomorphic Killing form, and define an explicit, mapping class group invariant, complex hyperK\"ahler structure on such deformation space. Such complex hyperK\"ahler structure restricts to: Donaldson's hyperK\"ahler structure on a totally real copy of almost-Fuchsian space, Mazzoli-Seppi-Tamburelli's para-hyperK\"ahler structure on a totally real copy of maximally globally hyperbolic $\mathbb{A}\mathrm{d}\mathbb{S}^3$ manifolds, and Loustau-Sanders' complex bi-K\"ahler structure on a holomorphic copy of quasi-Fuchsian space. Moreover, all these loci are totally geodesic. We discuss other geometric aspects of this space, such as the Hamiltonian property of a natural $\mathbb{C}^*$-action, involving the Goldman symplectic form and a complex-valued area functional.
item.dc:creator: Christian El Emam, Filippo Mazzoli, Nicholas Rungi, Andrea Seppi, Andrea Tamburelli

item.title: Non-symmetric vector dyson equations
item.description: arXiv:2607.16333v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the vector Dyson equation $$-\frac{1}{m(z)}=z\mathbf{1}-\mathbf{a}+Sm(z),$$ with parameter $z$ in the complex upper half-plane $\mathbb{C}_+$, where $\mathbf{a}\in\mathbb R^d$ and $S$ is a nonnegative matrix, not necessarily symmetric. This equation has a unique vector solution $m(z)\in\mathbb{C}_+^d$, for which we establish a complete measure decomposition and prove regularity. We then develop a graph-theoretic approach to the singularity and stability problem for non-symmetric matrices $S$. The graph structure of $S$ identifies the possible degeneracies of the stability operator as $z$ approaches the real axis. In particular, for non-backtracking matrices, we prove square-root growth at regular edges, cubic-root growth at regular cusps, and complete stability estimates. We also obtain the corresponding estimates for symmetric matrices in the periodic setting.
item.dc:creator: Jiaoyang Huang, Zhonggen Su, Ruizhe Xu

item.title: Jacobi Endpoint Pencils and Sharp Interlacing for Centered Binomial Samples
item.description: arXiv:2608.08714v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study interlacing between real polynomial quotients obtained from centered binomial samples of a fixed even or odd real entire function at consecutive odd degrees. For sources of order at most one, we determine the optimal vertical-strip half-widths guaranteeing weak interlacing for every adjacent pair: $\sqrt{15/28}$ for even sources and the explicit algebraic constant $h_*\approx 1.0656$ for odd sources. These constants are forced by the first nontrivial pair and suffice at every degree. Under the same sharp bounds, nonpolynomial sources have simple zeros in $(-2,2)$ and strict interlacing at every positive index. We also prove an eventual result: if a nonpolynomial source has growth order less than two and only finitely many zeros off the imaginary axis, then all sufficiently high adjacent quotients have simple interior zeros and strictly interlace; the starting index depends only on the finite factor formed from those zeros. The proof turns the sampling problem into an interval real-rootedness problem for a Jacobi differential operator. For fixed degree, we also determine the maximal range of scalar shifts preserving real-rooted polynomials with at most one zero outside the interval. Applications give strict interlacing for quotients attached to completed Dedekind zeta derivatives and to successive centered blocks of critical values of self-dual newforms satisfying explicit spacing and parity conditions.
item.dc:creator: Seokho Jin

item.title: Local-to-global maximality for plurisubharmonic functions with locally analytic singularities
item.description: arXiv:2610.05937v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that a locally maximal plurisubharmonic function on a domain in $\bC^n$, $n\geq2$, is maximal if it has locally analytic singularities with a two-sided locally bounded remainder. Using McAdam's theorem, we show that local maximality forces the analytic spread of each defining ideal to be less than $n$. We use normalized blow-ups and Siu's analyticity theorem to compare singularities through generic divisorial Lelong numbers. We also obtain a criterion for maximality in terms of maximality outside the pole set and the analytic spread of the local defining ideals.
item.dc:creator: Thai Duong Do, Pham Hoang Hiep

item.title: Sharp Subordination Radii through Boundary Minimization
item.description: arXiv:2610.12006v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\varphi$ and $\psi$ be univalent functions in the unit disk $\mathbb D$ satisfying $\varphi(0)=\psi(0)=1$ and $\varphi\not\prec\psi$, and let $\mathcal P_{\varphi}$ denote the class of analytic functions $p$ in $\mathbb D$ such that $p\prec\varphi$. Under suitable analytic continuation, univalence, and boundary-behavior hypotheses on the branch of $\varphi^{-1}$ satisfying $\varphi^{-1}(1)=0$, we determine the sharp $\mathcal P_{\psi}$-radius of $\mathcal P_{\varphi}$ as \[ \mathcal R(\varphi,\psi) = \min_{|\zeta|=1} \left| \varphi^{-1}\bigl(\psi(\zeta)\bigr) \right|. \] For Ma--Minda functions satisfying these hypotheses, the same radius is sharp for the associated classes $\mathcal{ST}(\varphi)$ and $\mathcal{CV}(\varphi)$ with respect to $\mathcal{ST}(\psi)$ and $\mathcal{CV}(\psi)$, respectively. We apply the general result to $ \varphi_{\mathrm L}(z)=\sqrt{1+z}, \varphi_{\mathrm{\leftmoon}}(z)=z+\sqrt{1+z^2}, \varphi_{\mathrm{Lim}}(z)=\left(1+{z}/{\sqrt2}\right)^2, $ for several choices of the Ma--Minda function $\psi$, and obtain parameter-dependent extensions for the corresponding generalized families. The resulting boundary minima are evaluated analytically.
item.dc:creator: Poomalai Palanisamy, Ravichandran Vaithiyanathan

item.title: Maximum-modulus points on concentric circles
item.description:
arXiv:2610.15067v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a negative answer to the second question of Erd\H{o}s Problem #1117: can the number $
u_f(r)$ of maximum-modulus points of a nonzero, non-monomial entire function on $|z|=r$ tend to infinity as $r	o\infty$? Write $f(z)=z^m g(z)$ with $g(0)
e0$, and let $k$ be the first positive exponent with a nonzero coefficient in the Taylor expansion of $g$. We prove that $\{r>0:
u_f(r)>2k\}$ is locally finite in $(0,\infty)$, and that the constant $2k$ is sharp. In particular, $\liminf_{r	o\infty}
u_f(r)\le2k<\infty$, without a growth assumption. The proof combines finite local parametrizations of a logarithmic-derivative correspondence with analytic continuation and a local description of stationary points.
item.dc:creator: Yunpeng Li

item.title: On the fundamental groups of subelliptic varieties
item.description: arXiv:2212.07085v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that the fundamental group of any smooth subelliptic variety is finite. Moreover, it is also proved that every finite group can be realized as the fundamental group of a smooth subelliptic variety. As a consequence, it follows that there exists a smooth subelliptic variety homotopy equivalent to the $n$-sphere if and only if $n>1$. This result can be considered as a negative answer to the algebraic version of Gromov's problem on the homotopy types of Oka manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Yuta Kusakabe

item.title: Matrix-valued regular functions of a quaternionic variable - a decomposition and some approximation results
item.description: arXiv:2510.07866v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A quaternionic matrix-valued regular function is a map $F: \Omega \rightarrow M_n(\mathbb{H})$ whose entries are (left) regular functions of a quaternion variable, where $\Omega$ is a domain in $\mathbb{H}$. Given any $n \times n$ matrix-valued regular function $F(q)$ over $\mathbb{H}$ having norm at most $1$, we derive a decomposition of $F(q)$ in the form $U \star \begin{bmatrix} ||F(q_0)|| & 0\\0 & G(q)\end{bmatrix} V$ for some constant unitary matrices $U, V$, some vector $q_0$ and an $(n-1) \times (n-1)$ matrix-valued regular function $G(q)$, where $\star$ denotes the star product over $\mathbb{H}$. We use this to deduce that any matrix-valued regular function $F(q)$ having norm at most $1$ can be uniformly approximated by a convex combination of rational unitary functions.
item.dc:creator: T. P. Dhashna, Sachindranath Jayaraman

item.title: Inner Products and Banach Algebra structures on Bicomplex Numbers and Their Associated Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2607.06543v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we introduce various types of inner products and norms on the bicomplex number system $\mathbb{C}_2$, the bicomplex vector space ${\mathbb{C}_2}^{n}$, the space of bicomplex matrices ${C_2}^{m \times n}$, and the space of bicomplex polynomials $\mathbb{C}_2[\xi]_n$. We investigate the relationships among these inner products and norms, and establish several results. Furthermore, we prove that $\mathbb{C}_2$ and ${\mathbb{C}_2}^{n}$ are Banach algebras and Hilbert spaces. These results provide a unified framework for the study of inner product structures and normed linear spaces over bicomplex numbers and their associated spaces.
item.dc:creator: Prabhat Kumar, Fahed Zulfeqarr, Amit Ujlayan, Anjali Anjali, Akhil Prakash, M. Younus Bhat

item.title: Hyperbolic area of Fatou components and new proofs of no-wandering-domain theorems
item.description: arXiv:2609.23834v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a new elementary proof of Sullivan's no-wandering-domain theorem for rational maps of degree at least two using hyperbolic area. We then develop this method further to prove that a transcendental entire function has no wandering Fatou components if its set of singular values is compact and all accumulation points of that set lie in the Fatou set. Neither proof uses quasiconformal techniques.
item.dc:creator: Zihao Ye

item.title: Non-autonomous dynamics of inner functions: mixing and entropy
item.description: arXiv:2609.31476v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We generalise a mixing result due to Pommerenke for non-autonomous dynamical systems of forward compositions of the boundary values of centred inner functions; the proof depends on a precise bound on the orbits of such forward compositions in the unit disc. This enables us to give new criteria for such systems to have positive metric entropy, lower entropy and topological entropy. In the opposite direction, we construct a forward composition of centred degree two Blaschke products with topological entropy zero.
item.dc:creator: Vasiliki Evdoridou, N\'uria Fagella, Philip Rippon, Gwyneth Stallard

item.title: The strong reproducing kernel thesis for Hankel operators and the Garsia norm
item.description: arXiv:2609.33242v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given a reproducing kernel Hilbert space $\mathcal H$ and a bounded operator $T$ on $\mathcal H$, we say that $T$ obeys the strong reproducing kernel thesis (SRKT) if $\|T\|=\sup_k\|Tk\|$, where $k$ ranges over the normalized reproducing kernels in $\mathcal H$. Two problems are posed. One of these is to determine which Hankel operators on the Hardy space $H^2$ obey the SRKT. The other concerns the geometry of the unit ball of $BMO$ with respect to the Garsia norm.
item.dc:creator: Konstantin M. Dyakonov

item.title: Plane wave representations for wave scattering on a sphere
item.description: arXiv:2610.15121v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Motivated by three-dimensional wave diffraction by conical shapes, we consider the two-dimensional problem of wave scattering on the real sphere $\mathcal{S}^2$ resulting from a point-source incidence on a scatterer $\mathbb{S}$. Using the recently introduced notion of plane waves on $\mathcal{S}^2$ as well as recent results on the Laplace--Beltrami Green's function $G$ on $\mathcal{S}^2$, we derive three plane-wave representations for the scattered field $u$. We then explain how $u$ can be analytically continued to the complexified sphere $\mathcal{S}^2_{\mathbb{c}}$. This allows us to formulate a complexified version of Green's third identity, and to provide a characterisation of complex sources. All our results are then used to draw strong analogies between planar and spherical scattering problems, notably through the introduction of directivities.
item.dc:creator: Valentin D. Kunz, Andrey V. Shanin, Raphael C. Assier
